plan.contextChunk: This figure is an oblique three-dimensional drawing of a disk drive, rendered as line art with gray shading and five callout labels. Two circular platters are stacked one above the other, each a flat gray disk with visible edge thickness; a leader from the upper left points to the top disk and reads "platter." A dark vertical rod runs through the centers of both disks and protrudes above and below the stack, tagged "spindle" by an arrow at the top. A long curved arrow sweeping across the top surface toward the upper right gives the direction in which the platters turn. Drawn concentrically on the top platter, partway between the spindle and the rim, is a heavy gray circle labeled "track." A small solid black tip resting on that circle is labeled "read/write head"; it sits at the end of a slender tapered arm that extends to the right and broadens into a rounded pad. A second arm of identical shape reaches the lower platter, and the two pads are joined by a short vertical post serving as their shared pivot, with two leaders below marked "arms." A double-headed arrow beside the head shows the arm swinging toward and away from the spindle. Separating the spin of the platters from the radial swing of the arms makes plain how any point of a magnetized surface is brought under a head. The drawing lays out the mechanical parts of the storage device and fixes the names used for them.

elements: upper circular platter drawn as a flat light-gray cylinder with black elliptical outline and visible thin edge
lower circular platter drawn directly below the upper platter as a matching light-gray cylinder with black elliptical outline and visible edge
dark vertical spindle rod passing through the center of both platters and protruding above and below the stack
single selected concentric track on the upper platter drawn as a thick gray ring
additional faint concentric track guide rings on the upper platter
small dark sector/tick marks attached to the selected track so disk rotation is visible
solid black read/write head resting on the selected track on the upper-right portion of the upper platter
long upper tapered actuator arm extending from the right-side pivot assembly to the read/write head
long lower tapered actuator arm extending from the same pivot assembly toward the lower platter
rounded oval pad at the right end of the upper actuator arm
rounded oval pad at the right end of the lower actuator arm
short vertical pivot post joining the two arm pads
curved black arrows on the upper platter showing platter spin direction
curved double-headed sweep arrow near the read/write head showing the radial seek motion of the arm
text label 'platter' at upper left with a leader arrow to the upper platter
text label 'spindle' above the center with a leader arrow to the spindle rod
text label 'track' above the platter with a leader arrow to the highlighted concentric ring
text label 'read/write head' at upper right with a leader arrow to the black head
text label 'arms' at lower right with two leader arrows pointing to the upper and lower actuator arms

interactions.label: Arm angle
interactions.teaches: Seeking is radial: swinging the actuator arm moves the read/write head from an outer track toward an inner track near the spindle while the platters remain centered in place

interactions.label: Spin platter
interactions.teaches: Once the head is positioned over a track, rotation brings different angular positions, or sectors, of that same track underneath the stationary head

demo_steps.title: Outer track selected
demo_steps.narration: The actuator arm is swung outward, placing the read/write head near the rim. The highlighted track is large because the head is selecting a large radius.

demo_steps.title: Middle track selected
demo_steps.narration: Swinging the arm inward moves the head across the disk surface without moving the platter stack. The selected track follows the head's radius.

demo_steps.title: Inner track selected
demo_steps.narration: Near the spindle, the same angular rotation covers a smaller circular track. Playing the spin animation shows sectors passing under the fixed head after the seek is complete.

interactionPlan.geometry_notes: Use an oblique line-art style matching the source. World coordinates: +X is screen-right across the platter, +Y is the vertical spindle/stack direction, and +Z is the receding disk-depth direction that becomes the ellipse minor axis in the drawing. Platters are two shallow cylinders centered at (0,0,0) and (0,-0.75,0), each radius 4.0 units in the XZ plane and thickness about 0.14 units in Y; upper platter top surface is near y=0.07, lower platter top surface near y=-0.68. Draw black outlines on top and bottom ellipses plus a darker front edge line. Spindle is a dark gray vertical cylinder at x=0,z=0 with radius 0.045, extending from y=-1.45 to y=1.25. Pivot assembly is to the right of the platters at approximately x=5.2,z=0,y=-0.35; the vertical pivot post radius is 0.08 and extends from y=-0.95 to y=0.25. Upper and lower arm pads are flattened oval disks/capsules about 1.25 units long in X and 0.65 units wide in Z, centered near x=5.15,z=0 at y=0.18 and y=-0.72. Top arm lies just above the upper platter at y=0.16; lower arm lies near y=-0.62 and is partially visible beneath the top platter. Model each arm as a tapered gray strip with black outline, narrow at the head end and wider at the pivot end. Arm/head kinematics: let pivot P=(5.2,0) in the XZ disk plane, arm length L=4.0, and alpha = 45 degrees - armSweepAngle; head position H = P + L*(-cos(alpha), sin(alpha)). With armSweepAngle=0 the head is on an outer track of radius about 3.7; with armSweepAngle=30 the head is on an inner track of radius about 1.7. The highlighted track radius is r=sqrt(H.x^2+H.z^2), centered on the spindle. Place the black read/write head as a small flattened sphere or disk of radius 0.16 at H on the upper platter surface. Add faint guide tracks at radii 1.6, 2.1, 2.6, 3.1, and 3.6, with only the selected track thick and dark. Colors: platter fill #e6e6e6, platter outlines #111111, selected track #808080, faint tracks #bdbdbd, spindle #6f6f6f, arms and pads #9c9c9c, head #000000, arrows and labels #000000. Text labels should be large black serif labels positioned like the source: 'platter' upper left, 'spindle' upper center, 'track' above the selected ring, 'read/write head' upper right, and 'arms' lower right.
interactionPlan.notes: Use an orthographic oblique rendering with crisp black outlines and simple flat gray materials. Keep labels as screen-facing text sprites with leader lines and triangular arrowheads so they remain readable. For the spin animation, rotate only the platter surface markings, selected-track tick marks, and optional subtle texture marks about the spindle; the platter centers, spindle, pivot, arms, and read/write head should not translate. Recompute the head position, upper/lower arm taper geometry, selected track radius, and leader arrow endpoints whenever the arm slider changes.

authoredContext:
Figure 18.2 shows a typical disk drive. The drive consists of one or more platters, which rotate at a constant speed around a common spindle. A magnetizable material covers the surface of each platter. The drive reads and writes each platter by a head at the end of an arm. The arms can move their heads toward or away from the spindle. When a given head is stationary, the surface that passes underneath it is called a track. Multiple platters increase only the disk drive’s capacity
and not its performance.
